_: Region sheet for mercantile-coast (2.5a1b). Talk is seeded from the region's published place records; every trait cites a lore dossier or says inferred.

entries.name: Lilmoth and the south coast (the mercantile coast)

norms.text: A merchant council runs the port; old offices and new holders.
Unlicensed foreigners stay on the docks, by a law some officials still enforce.
Prices are given in drakes; a hard thing is called business.
Disputes go to an arbitrator both sides choose, usually a tree-minder or a retired Shadowscale.

taboos.text: Building in the drowned Old Imperial quarter; it is a grave.
Communing with the young Hist alone; a second tender is always present.

values.text: Two tenders at the Hist, always.
A licence on paper with a crew that will work under its terms.

contempts.text: The An-Xileel, who killed Lilmoth with its own tree.
Ships' owners who send crews into the reefs and write off the loss.

place.text: The coast is built on stilts over the old city; people live on it anyway.

work.text: Lightering, salvage and the stage roads keep the coast fed.

people.text: Two names for every place and two crews for every hull.

faction.text: The Compact holds the boats and the council wants the licences.

hist.text: The new tree is tended and feared in equal measure.

empire.text: The Imperial quarter is under the water and stays there.

trade.text: Archon, Lilmoth, Soulrest and Tear: the old Company line still runs.

danger.text: Sea-drakes off the harbour and the mangrove wall inland.

rumour.text: Salvage turns up from ships whose owners do not know they sank.

directions.text: Ways are given by the coast: so many stages east, so many bends up the bay.

addressTerms.text: Merchants call each other by house or hull; customers are friend until they owe.
Clerks use the exonym and the Argonian quarter uses the verb-name.

neverSaid.text: The names of those who sided with the Hist of Lilmoth in 4E 48.

grievances.text: The council tried to license lightering and the crews stopped the port for two weeks.
No stage-keeper at Chasepoint has been paid in two centuries, but two families claim the office.

rumours.text: A faction says it knows the purpose for which the Teeth of Sithis was built.
The third Hist has started to dream.

views.text: Blackrose sends cargo and debtors down the river in the same boat.
Raiders from the deeps work the inland tracks; coast merchants pay for quiet.
Archon's harbour folk are rivals on the water and fair dealers ashore.
